title: Cap. III Rej. Rat. 1 close: electing will causes merits — sum before Rat. 2
pass_a_gloss: This is clear from this, because this very gratuitous will of God which precedes our merits or good works is the cause of these merits: How then shall we say that that will of God which is presupposed to merits is common, equal, and indifferent as to all, when in some it effects these very things which are called merits, in others it does not effect them? A distinction appears manifest in the effect; therefore it is understood also in the cause itself. Let us hear again Augustine speaking (whom we can never hear enough): True grace of God is that which is not given according to our merits, but which gives the merits themselves when it is given, because it precedes man's good will, and does not find it in anyone's heart, but makes it. Thus therefore this is the sum of our response: That will of God which precedes the foreknowledge of good works is not equal or indifferent concerning the salvation of all, seeing that in some God wills to produce these works of grace which lead to glory, in others he does not will: Therefore they badly infer that the efficacious will of God concerning giving salvation to the elect begins from the foresight of merits, when that [will] manifestly puts itself forth in that will of giving these very merits, which will preceded the foresight of merits, and ordained these very merits of theirs to salvation.
pass_b_english: Clear why: that free will of God before our merits or good works is itself their cause. How then call the will presupposed to merits common, equal, and indifferent to all, when in some it effects those "merits" and in others not? Effect differs; so does the cause. Hear Augustine again (never enough): true grace is not given by our merits but gives the merits when given — it goes before a good will, finds it in no heart, and makes it. Sum of our answer: the divine will before foresight of good works is not equal or indifferent about everyone's salvation, since in some God wills grace-works that lead to glory and in others he does not. So they wrongly start the efficacious saving will for the elect from foresight of merits — that will already shows itself in willing to give those merits, which will came before merit-foresight and ordered those merits to salvation.
source_text: Hoc ex eo liquet, quia haec ipsa gratuita voluntas Dei, quae praecedit merita sive bona opera nostra, est causa horum meritorum: Quomodo igitur dicamus illam Dei voluntatem quae meritis praesupponitur esse communem, aequalem & indifferentem quoad omnes, cum in aliquibus efficiat haec ipsa quae vocantur merita, in aliis non efficiat? Manifestum apparet discrimen in effectu; ergo intelligitur etiam in ipsa causa. Audiamus iterum (quem nunquam satis audire possumus) loquentem Augustinum: Vera Dei gratia est, quae non secundum merita nostra datur, sed quae dat merita ipsa cum datur, quia praevenit hominis voluntatem bonam, nec eam cujusquam invenit in corde, sed facit. Sic itaque haec summa responsionis nostrae: Non esse aequalem aut indifferentem de omnium salute illam Dei voluntatem, quae antecedit praescientiam bonorum operum, quandoquidem in aliquibus vult Deus producere haec opera gratiae, quae ducant ad gloriam, in aliis non vult: Male ergo inferunt, ex praevisione meritorum incipere efficacem Dei voluntatem de danda salute electis, cum ea manifeste se exerat in illa voluntate dandi haec ipsa merita, quae voluntas praevisionem meritorum praecessit, atque ad salutem haec ipsa illorum merita ordinavit.
